title: Helpers--Production Workers
description: Help production workers by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include supplying or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

tasks.text: Turn valves to regulate flow of liquids or air, to reverse machines, to start pumps, or to regulate equipment.
Remove products, machine attachments, or waste material from machines.
Tie products in bundles for further processing or shipment, following prescribed procedures.
Unclamp and hoist full reels from braiding, winding, or other fabricating machines, using power hoists.
Pack and store materials and products.
Prepare raw materials for processing.
Position spouts or chutes of storage bins so that containers can be filled.
Break up defective products for reprocessing.
Cut or break flashing from materials or products.
Load and unload items from machines, conveyors, and conveyances.
Place products in equipment or on work surfaces for further processing, inspecting, or wrapping.
Mix ingredients according to specified procedures or formulas.
Transfer finished products, raw materials, tools, or equipment between storage and work areas of plants and warehouses, by hand or using hand trucks or powered lift trucks.
Clean and lubricate equipment.
Help production workers by performing duties of lesser skill, such as supplying or holding materials or tools, or cleaning work areas and equipment.
Wash work areas, machines, equipment, vehicles, or products.
Operate machinery used in the production process, or assist machine operators.
Start machines or equipment to begin production processes.
Lift raw materials, finished products, and packed items, manually or using hoists.
Attach slings, ropes, or cables to objects such as pipes, hoses, or bundles.
Count finished products to determine if product orders are complete.
Examine products to verify conformance to quality standards.
Record information, such as the number of products tested, meter readings, or dates and times of product production.
Read gauges or charts, and record data obtained.

clusters.label: Estimating the Quantifiable Characteristics of Products, Events, or Information

tasks.text: Measure amounts of products, lengths of extruded articles, or weights of filled containers to ensure conformance to specifications.
Separate products according to weight, grade, size, or composition of materials used to produce them.
Mark or tag identification on parts.
Observe equipment operations so that malfunctions can be detected, and notify operators of any malfunctions.
Signal coworkers to direct them to move products during the production process.
Perform minor repairs to machines, such as replacing damaged or worn parts.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Operation and Control
skills.def: Controlling operations of equipment or systems.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Document management software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or search documents or files from other software or from paper copies. Examples: Adobe Acrobat.

skills.name: Desktop publishing software
skills.def: Software to create or edit text and graphics into documents such as books, magazines, brochures, or manuals. Examples: Adobe InDesign.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Photoshop.

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: Autodesk AutoCAD.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.
